Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract and the two applicable skills: the required fish-control transfer shelf, plus the visual-evidence skill that governs policy edits. Then I’ll inspect the current rollout artifacts before touching `solver/`.

The skills require a visual-first pass: I’ll compare the best finite rollout with the most informative contrasting example, verify still-water initialization, and cross-check each image-based claim against metrics and diagnostics. Only after that will I consult the bookshelf references and choose whether a transferable mechanism is justified.

The visual evidence is unusually consistent: all four samples are direct-uniform still-water captures, three reproducing the same 18.403 T path and one reaching capture 0.011 T later. Both views show a smooth target-directed arc with a coherent alternating wake and no visible loss of self-propulsion. Since there is no sampled failure sheet, the honest contrast is the slightly regressed response-release capture; I’m now quantifying where it differs before proposing a new mechanism.

The response-release variant is a concrete negative result: it leaves speed/load essentially unchanged while delaying capture and worsening both total and observed distance integrals. I’ll preserve the geometry-only divergence gate. The only prior positive mechanism with a localized, interpretable deficit is carrier-phase × crossflow pose rejection: it hurt at 8–14 T but helped from 16 T onward, so the candidate hypothesis is to activate that sensing correction only on late approach. The bookshelf consultation will now test whether that gating has a defensible invariant rather than serving as gain tuning.

The shelf supports a compact combination already suggested by the rollout: keep slow target geometry as route authority, treat alternating self-wake/crossflow only as a bounded sensing correction, and schedule that correction by the terminal capture regime. It does not justify changing frequency, amplitude, or copying a wake phase. I’ll read the corresponding source notes next, as the skill requires when a source family informs the edit.

The inherited terminal-only result is now fully resolved: it captures at 18.3865 T—better than geometry-only but later than full-route crossflow—while achieving the best observed distance integral of the three. That means distance scheduling successfully removed the middle-route cost but switched the useful correction on too late to retain its full arrival benefit. I’m testing a state-semantic gate next: admit the fast flow-based pose correction only when it agrees with slow body-frame target geometry, rather than using another fixed distance threshold.

The state audit supports the consistency gate: the full crossflow residual points toward the de-gaited target centerline on only ~39% of carrier states near 8 T, but ~68% near 16 T and ~61% near 18 T. I’ll record that hypothesis and the required bookshelf transfer block now, before editing the policy as required by the visual-first protocol.

The candidate now keeps the validated carrier and divergence recovery unchanged and adds one bounded observation-side selector: the crossflow/phase residual is applied only on carrier states where it contracts the slower de-gaited target bearing. I’m validating schema, finite bounds, reflection symmetry, and the intended activation pattern without running CFD.

The first reflection test hit a test-harness issue—Julia tuples do not support unary negation—not a policy error. The include and parameter scan completed, with no missing direct parameter names. I’m correcting the harness and rerunning the behavioral checks.

The corrected harness exposed an inherited property: the full controller is not exactly reflection-equivariant because its established positive/negative steering authority is intentionally asymmetric. I won’t mislabel that as a new defect. I’m narrowing the check to what this edit must preserve: the selector itself is sign-symmetric under reflected bearing/crossflow, and all resulting two-joint commands remain finite and bounded across the completed trace.

The offline audit passes: all 3,346 reconstructed states produce finite commands inside the unchanged acceleration envelope; 61 referenced parameters are present among 63 returned fields; the selector is reflection-symmetric on its own; and it activates on 56.4% of states with a realized correction capped at 1.49°. I’ll now turn the completed v34/v36/v37 evidence into a durable guidance lesson without claiming this unevaluated candidate as a result.

The visual-evidence and bookshelf skills have now shaped the actual edit: the change is confined to normalized body-frame pose sensing and is explicitly falsifiable against arrival, integral, wake coherence, and the established action/load envelope. I’m invoking the workspace’s mandated read-only check runner now.

The configured check-runner could not start because its pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unavailable for this account. The check instructions themselves are local and read-only, so I’m executing the same three mandated commands separately as the fallback and will repair any failure.

The first mandated check found a malformed rendered README: the same assigned parent ID is marked “copied to guidance” twice, so the checker rejects the workspace before comparing my guidance change. There is no parent ambiguity—the two matches are identical. I’m correcting only the duplicate marker in the workspace metadata, then rerunning the exact check; the assigned parent and guidance content remain unchanged.

All three mandated checks pass after the metadata repair: the notes/guidance semantic check, the lightweight Julia policy contract check, and the solver boundary check. No CFD was run. I’m doing a final inventory of the changed workspace files and then I’ll hand off the single candidate.

Produced exactly one candidate: [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:11).

- Adds a bounded, body-frame crossflow/phase pose correction only when it contracts the slower de-gaited target bearing.
- Recorded visual diagnosis, bookshelf transfer, and falsification criteria in [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1).
- Materially revised the reusable crossflow-scheduling lesson in [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:142).
- Removed one duplicate assigned-parent listing from [README.md](README.md:123) that prevented the mandated checker from parsing the workspace.

The configured check-runner model was unavailable, so I executed its exact three checks locally. Guidance semantics, Julia policy contract, parameter schema, and solver boundary all pass. No CFD was run.
